subject: Request: prorated account adjustment for delayed multi-model launch (exec approval needed)
messages:
From: Emma Walker <emma.walker@brightcart.com>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: raj.patel@brightcart.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightCart go-live timing + MAA timeline

Hi Sergio,

Quick update from our side — engineering pushed the multi-model routing work out of the June milestone. The feature is the last dependency for our personalization rollout, so the overall product launch is slipping by ~6 weeks.

I know the commitment in our MAA assumed multi-model support would be available by end of June. With the delay, we’re seeing lower ROI on the committed capacity and would like to discuss a short-term commercial accommodation — specifically a prorated credit applied to our June/July invoices or a temporary reduction to committed pricing while the feature is delivered.

I attached a short usage snapshot for May to show current consumption vs committed baseline. Happy to jump on a call, but wanted to put this in writing and outline the ask so your team has context.

Attachments: usage_report_May2026.csv

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Walker
Head of Platform & Ops | BrightCart
emma.walker@brightcart.com

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Emma Walker <emma.walker@brightcart.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightCart go-live timing + MAA timeline

Emma — thanks for the heads-up and for the usage snapshot. Sorry to hear the engineering delay is forcing the push.

Quick next steps from our side:
- I’ll pull finance and commercial into the thread (cc’d) to scope options (prorated invoice credit vs short-term committed-rate adjustment).
- Karthik — can you and Laura draft a recommended accommodation and list the approvals needed for a one-off? If it helps, BrightCart is proposing something that covers the two-month impact window.
- Emma / Raj — can you share the internal calendar for the revised launch so we can map exact billing periods?

We want to be reasonable here; we also need to protect the pricing guardrails we give other customers. I’ll coordinate an exec approval if finance/legal need sign-off.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: prorated account adjustment for delayed multi-model launch (exec approval needed)

Folks — I reviewed the usage file and the MAA terms. Proposal for discussion: a one-time prorated adjustment equal to 15% of BrightCart’s committed monthly spend for two billing cycles (June + July) OR a straight two-month credit equal to the average committed spend, whichever is simpler to apply operationally.

Rationale: strike a balance between making good on customer relations (they’re in active rollout and this is a timing issue) and maintaining a predictable commercial policy.

Requirements before we execute:
1) Executive sign-off on the amount (I’ll prepare an exec_decision_sheet.xlsx with scenarios).
2) SOW amendment or signed addendum documenting the acceptance of the accommodation and the revised delivery timeline.
3) Finance confirmation on invoicing path (credit memo vs. discount on future invoices).

Marissa — once we have the amount, can CS draft the customer-facing note? We should avoid terms that imply product failure.

I’ll attach a decision worksheet for clarity.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: prorated account adjustment for delayed multi-model launch (exec approval needed)

Thanks — a couple of operational notes from finance:
- We prefer issuing a credit memo applied to the next invoice cycle. That avoids carrying negative revenue and is easier for the revenue ops team.
- We need an SOW amendment signed (simple one-page addendum referencing the original MAA). Legal will need to confirm wording; Grace looped in.
- For accounting, please include the deal_id on the credit memo (BR-2026-0114) and provide an explicit amount and date ranges (e.g., "15% of committed monthly spend for June and July 2026").

If execs approve, finance can generate the credit within 3 business days of receiving the signed addendum and the approved exec_decision_sheet.xlsx.

Attachments referenced: MAA_BrightCart_SOW_v2.pdf (for SOW context)

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance | Redwood Inference

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, Emma Walker <emma.walker@brightcart.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@brightcart.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Final ask: exec sign-off request (BrightCart prorated accommodation)

Team — I’ve summarized the recommended option in the attached exec_decision_sheet.xlsx. TL;DR recommendation: approve a one-time credit equal to 15% of BrightCart’s committed monthly spend applied to June and July invoices (calculation in the sheet). Reasons: customer in active rollout, timing delay not caused by Redwood, high expansion potential (they are on the cusp of scaling personalization), and avoids churn risk.

If we get a yes from execs today, next steps:
- Laura to issue credit memo after signed addendum.
- Marissa to send the CS-approved communications to BrightCart (I’ll draft).
- Grace to confirm legal language for the SOW addendum (one page).

Emma / Raj — I propose we send the addendum (one-page) and the credit schedule for signature. If you’re ok, I’ll have our legal ops send a DocuSign link and our finance team will queue the credit memo.

Attachments: exec_decision_sheet.xlsx; MAA_BrightCart_SOW_v2.pdf
Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/BR-2026-0114

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
